selection_reasoning: Mining oak wood produces logs/planks that serve as the primary construction material for building a bridge. This creates a natural resource-gathering → construction dependency chain. The player must first obtain wood by mining oak trees, then use that wood to build a bridge across a gap (e.g., a river or ravine). Both tasks are visually observable and verifiable — oak wood inventory can be checked, and the bridge structure can be spatially verified. This avoids deep Minecraft domain knowledge while creating a meaningful multi-hop sequence.

edges.reason: Building a bridge requires oak planks/logs as construction material, obtained by mining oak trees first

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining oak_log blocks causes them to drop as oak_log items into the player's inventory. Checking for min_count=1 verifies the player has successfully mined at least one oak log, proving they can harvest wood. We intentionally keep this at 1 (not 6) because a player may mine logs incrementally and place them as they go — they may never hold 6 simultaneously. The bridge milestone separately verifies enough material was gathered and used.

Uses count_in_box_at_least (kind=block) because building a bridge means placing solid blocks over the water gap. The river spans z=5 to z=10 (spawn-relative, 6 blocks wide) after widening to prevent sprint-jumping. We check for oak_log blocks in a generous box: x=[-5,5] covers multiple possible bridge paths, y=[-1,1] allows placement at water surface or slightly above. min_count=6 ensures a complete spanning bridge (one block per z-coordinate). Only oak_log is checked because no crafting table is provided in the scene, making direct log placement the simplest and most likely strategy.

scene_description: A flat grassy area with two oak trees near the player spawn. A 6-block-wide river (z=5 to z=10) runs east-west, creating an impassable gap that cannot be sprint-jumped. A gold block landmark on the far side (z=12) motivates the player to build a bridge. The player is given an iron axe to efficiently mine the oak trees for wood, which they must then use to construct a bridge across the river.
task_text: Mine oak wood from the nearby trees using your iron axe, then use the wood to build a bridge across the river to reach the gold block on the other side.
design_notes: Player spawns at origin facing south. Two oak trees at (~3,~0,~2) and (~-3,~0,~1) provide 10 oak logs total. River spans z=5 to z=10 (6 blocks wide, 3 deep) — definitively too wide to sprint-jump. Gold block at z=12 serves as destination landmark. Iron axe given for efficient mining. Player must: 1) mine oak logs → get oak_log items, 2) place logs across the river as a bridge (minimum 6 blocks needed). No crafting table provided — simplest path is placing logs directly.
